source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper observes only pre-treatment covariates in the target population, states target-population IV assumptions and first-stage exchangeability, identifies T-CACE by a target-weighted Wald ratio, and develops regular weighted estimators.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2, Notation and Structural Causal Model
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The observed vector is O=(S,W,A,Z,S×Y): target-site assignment and receipt are observed while outcome is missing; the paper develops TMLEs for transported ITT, complier ATE, and exposure effects.
The paper extends weak-instrument-robust inference to two-sample IV regression and relaxes homoskedasticity and equal-moment restrictions across samples.

The paper is a weaktsiv implementation companion for two-sample linear IV; both samples contain instrument/covariate measurements, the second supplies the endogenous regressor, and AR/K/CLR confidence sets are inverted under weak-IV asymptotics.
The paper constructs weak-IV robust linear-IV confidence sets and establishes near-shortest expected arc length only among similar symmetric invariant sets in a circular model.
The paper studies one-population nonparametric score-test inversion for LATE, uniform validity with arbitrarily weak instruments, and confidence-set geometry including infinite diameter.
The paper proposes an orthogonalized Anderson–Rubin inversion procedure for high-dimensional one-population LATE with uniformly valid size irrespective of identification strength.

The paper treats finite-sample optimal ATE estimation and confidence intervals under unconfoundedness plus smoothness or shape restrictions, including limited overlap; it is not a weak-IV ratio result.
The paper studies regular doubly robust generalization and transportation of target ATEs, with convergence rates, limiting distributions, efficiency, and minimax results.
